summary: 1934 steel L-4 tower on Greenhorn Mountain that caught fires into the 1980s and is now a Sequoia National Forest rental cabin.

facts.design: L-4 cab, 14x14 ft, on a steel tower with catwalk

access.note: Recreation cabin rental; 4WD recommended for the final stretch of road.

visit.trail_note: Final approach is unimproved gravel road; last 0.7 miles up a spur road to the tower.

events.note: Newspaper reported construction of a new steel lookout tower on Oak Flat peak in September 1934; NHLR also lists 1934 as the build year.
Oak Flat lookout staff spotted the Rattlesnake Grade fire in July 1940.
Lookout guard Mrs. Andre Keown staffed the tower; radioed for emergency help after falling ill.
Recreation.gov describes the lookout as operational until the 1980s.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register March 8, 1999.
Closed to rental for the 2022 season for winter storm damage repairs.

evidence.supports: Build year, cab design, NHLR registration date, 2022 closure.
evidence.quote: The 14' x 14' L-4 cab with catwalk was constructed in 1934. It is now open to the public on the recreation cabin rental program. The lookout will be unavailable during the 2022 season to repair Winter storm damage.
The United States forest service is building a new steel lookout tower on Oak Flat peak six miles below Davis ranger station on Greenhorn Mountain.

The Rattlesnake grade fire this morning was discovered by the Oak Flat lookout post. Twelve county firemen and 20 men from a prison camp in the vicinity were detailed to fight the fire, bringing it under control within two hours.

evidence.supports: 1945 staffing and emergency evacuation of lookout guard, including the fire control assistant and her daughter.
evidence.quote: An emergency call Wednesday sent Sequoia National Forest service officials into action when they answered an S.O.S. from the Greenhorn district's only woman fire lookout guard, Mrs. Andre Keown, stationed at Oak Flat. ... District Ranger R.F. Droege in turn radioed the Fulton ranger station and dispatched Allen Sheldon, fire control assistant, to Mrs. Keown's station. Mr. Sheldon rushed to the Oak Flat lookout point and brought Mrs. Keown to Bakersfield... Her daughter, Donna, 4, stays at the lookout point with her.
Oak Flat Lookout was constructed in 1934 to provide fire detection views along the Kern River Canyon...The lookout was operational until the 1980s.

evidence.supports: Access logistics: no electricity/water, pulley system, 40 steps.
evidence.quote: There is no electricity or water in the lookout. All provisions, including food, water and bedding, must be carried up 40 steep steps to the tower space or pulled hand-over-hand in a small basket pulley system.

notes_for_editor: No source consulted gave a tower height in meters, so height_m was omitted from facts rather than filled with the elevation figure.
